content.intro: Learn queryset evaluation and laziness through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: QuerySet Evaluation and Laziness matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: Visual guide: QuerySet Evaluation and Laziness
content_blocks.alt_text: A QuerySet generally delays database work until evaluation; repeated use of the same evaluated QuerySet may use its result cache.
content_blocks.caption: Use this visual to connect QuerySet Evaluation and Laziness to the broader flow; it is an overview, not a substitute for the worked example.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines queryset evaluation and laziness as part of the django orm and querysets. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Lazy query execution; Evaluation triggers; QuerySet caching; Iteration; Avoiding unnecessary evaluations. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Lazy query execution
items.text: Lazy query execution should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: QuerySet caching
items.text: A QuerySet describes database operations and is commonly lazy. Build filters and ordering before evaluation; use the database to narrow results rather than pulling everything into Python.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: QuerySet Evaluation and Laziness
content_blocks.code:
books = Book.objects.filter(published_year__gte=2020)  # usually no query yet
count = books.count()  # sends a count query
first_book = books.first()  # may send a separate query
content_blocks.expected_output: QuerySets are lazy, but evaluation triggers database work; a count and a later iteration are not automatically the same query.
